title: Revised Curriculum for Degree Programs in Computer Science (BS CS, Associate Degree Computing) 2025
summary: HEC notifies the revised Computer Science curriculum (NQF levels 5 and 6), aligned with the HEC Undergraduate Education Policy V1.1 (2023). All universities offering these programs must align their curriculum with it as the minimum benchmark; departments develop course contents within the framework. Copied to the Chairman NCEAC.

files.caption: Program structure and course load, page 14
Semester VIII and internship note, page 20

clauses.quote: The revised curriculum for disciplines under the domain of Computer Science is hereby notified. All universities offering these programs are required to align their Computer Science curriculum with these updated standards/framework as the minimum benchmark for quality and compliance.

Computing programs prepare students to attain educational objectives by ensuring that students demonstrate achievement of the following outcomes (derived from Graduate Attributes defined by Seoul Accord): 1 Academic Education … 10 Life-long Learning.
Course Load (per semester): 15-21 credit hours for regular semesters. 1 Credit Hour (Practical Work) requires three contact hours per week throughout the semester.
The suggestive scheme of studies for BS Computer Science program is given below (Semester I – VIII, 130 credit hours).

Internships of three (03) credit hours must be completed in accordance with HEC Undergraduate Education Policy V 1.1. This requirement cannot be substituted with additional coursework, capstone, research, or project work.

title: Accreditation Manual of the National Computing Education Accreditation Council (Second Edition)
summary: NCEAC's accreditation manual: the accreditation process, the Self-Assessment Report, and the nine standards (criteria) based on Seoul Accord Document D.5 — program objectives, graduate attributes, curriculum and learning process, students, faculty, facilities, institutional support, continuous improvement and industrial linkages.

clauses.quote: A comprehensive set of standards have been developed by NCEAC based on Seoul Accord Document D.5 … Criterion-1 Program Objectives; Criterion-2 Graduate Attributes; Criterion-3 Curriculum and Learning Process; Criterion-4 Students; Criterion-5 Faculty and Support Staff; Criterion-6 Facilities and Infrastructure; Criterion-7 Institutional Support and Financial Resources; Criterion-8 Steps to Improve the Program; Criterion-9 Industrial Linkages.

Graduate attributes are statements that describe the set of skills, knowledge, and attitude that institute expects from its graduates … GAs defined by NCEAC are in alignment with the Graduate Attributes laid down in the Seoul Accord document D.5 for computing professionals.
